**SEED-1 (gold-moving).** Both worlds keep one continuous Part A episode across a hospital absence of three midnights — task 0: departure 2026-09-26 18:40, return 09-29 (bed-hold 1431d92d); task 1: departure 10-26 19:05, return 10-29 (0342fd8c). `qualifying_stay_and_transfer_windows_7fdf5798`: "Interrupted-stay window: consecutive calendar days within which a return to the same center continues the same coverage episode | 3 days (return by 12:00 a.m. of the third day)"; `one_open_episode_rule_e2edacbc`: "a return after that window opens a new episode once the earlier one has ended"; `nomnc_and_coverage_end_96dd9af5`: coverage ends without NOMNC "when a hospital transfer is not followed by a return within the interrupted-stay window (hospital transfer, no return)". Counting the departure day as day 1 (the PDPM interrupted-stay convention the charter cites) the window is 26–28 (task 0) / 26–28 (task 1); counting from the day after departure, a return on the third day comes after "12:00 a.m. of the third day". Under either reading the return on the 29th is outside the window, so the published Medicare documents produce an ended episode (hospital transfer, no return) and a new episode from the 29th. Effect on Medicaid reads: task 0 — the actual-month review covers only a resident with "exactly one coverage episode under Medicare Part A" (two → no Oct reduction), and September fails "the month's Part A days were all booked by the resident's coverage with the latest coverage start" (→ not priced day by day; cost 24 × 287.36 = 6,896.64; no reconciliation reduction); task 1 — October fails the same test (→ cost 22 × 279.84 = 6,156.48; no reduction).
